message.content: {"caption":"A conceptual diagram contrasts rigid, predefined agent memory with memory that an agent learns to optimize and adapt for itself.","description":"The top workflow shows a person studying and pointing beside an open book, with a right-pointing arrow to a panel headed “Teaching the Agent how to optimize memory.” The panel lists three lessons with icons: “Understand goals” (light bulb), “Learn to evaluate what to remember” (brain-like icon), and “Learn to organize, update, and discard” (gear). A solid right-pointing arrow leads to a robot labeled “AGENT,” with a network-like brain symbol above it. A dashed right-pointing arrow labeled “Guided by principles” leads toward a section headed “Agent optimizes its own memory.” Four green checked items read “Select important info,” “Compress and structure,” “Update and adapt,” and “Forget what’s unimportant.” Beneath them, document icons are linked to a central blue database cylinder, illustrating organized memory and information links.\n\nThe lower half compares two approaches. The left panel, “Previous Work: Give a Fish,” says “Force the model to follow a predefined memory strategy or format.” A clipboard labeled “Predefined Strategy / Format” points right via an arrow labeled “Force” to a robot, which points right to a database labeled “Rigid Memory (hard to adapt).” A small thought-cloud-like symbol appears above the robot. The right panel, “Our Principle: Teach to Fish,” says “Teach the model how to optimize its memory.” A book labeled “Principles & Optimization Skills” points right to a robot, with a light-bulb symbol above it; a dashed right-pointing arrow leads from the robot to a database with surrounding linked document icons, labeled “Flexible Memory (more adaptive).” The comparison presents fixed instructions and rigid storage on the left versus learned principles and more adaptable memory on the right.","figure_type":"diagram","chart_values":[]}
